title: The Voice of a Generation: Martina Arroyo

beats.text: Martina Arroyo has died at age 90, leaving a legacy as a pioneer of the opera stage.
Growing up in Harlem, she learned piano from her mother and sang in local Baptist choirs.
In 1962, she first rose to prominence in Europe, performing in the world premiere of Momente.
By 1965, she became a leading soprano at the Metropolitan Opera, performing on the world's greatest stages.
Her performances of Verdi and Puccini heroines made her a known figure in the Italian spinto repertoire.
Before her fame, she worked as a social worker, finding fulfillment in helping people with their problems.
Her dedication to the arts was recognized in 2013 when she received a Kennedy Center Honor.
Teaching singing across the United States and Europe became her devotion in her later years.

facts.evidence: Arroyo first rose to prominence in Europe, performing in the world premiere of Karlheinz Stockhausen's Momente in 1962 and as a regular leading soprano at the Zurich Opera between 1963 and 1965.
